# SDGR — Technical Analysis Report (as of 2026-10-07)

## Executive Summary

Schrödinger, Inc. (SDGR) has undergone an extraordinary structural transformation over the past month. After a grinding downtrend that carried the stock from ~$20 in October 2025 to a low of $11.08 on 2026-03-27, and a prolonged base between $11–$16 through mid-August, the stock exploded higher starting 2026-09-14. In just three sessions (09-15 through 09-17) the price ran from $23.25 to a close of $30.24 — a ~55% move off the 09-10 close of $18.80, on massive volume (9.03M shares on 09-17 vs. a typical ~1M). Price peaked intraday at $33.78 on 2026-10-06 and has now pulled back sharply: the last two sessions dropped from $32.60 (10-05 close) to $28.90 and then $27.29 on 10-07, the latest verified close.

The tape now shows a violent, news-driven uptrend that is undergoing its first real correction. Trend structure remains strongly bullish (price far above all moving averages), but short-term momentum has flipped negative. This is a high-volatility, post-breakout consolidation environment — position sizing and stop discipline matter more than directional conviction.

## Indicator Selection and Rationale

Eight complementary indicators were selected to cover trend, momentum, volatility, and volume context:

- **close_50_sma** — medium-term trend anchor; now well below price, confirming the regime shift.
- **close_200_sma** — long-term benchmark; the rally has decisively reversed the prior secular downtrend.
- **close_10_ema** — fast trend line; price just broke below it, the first short-term warning.
- **macd / macdh** — MACD level shows the size of the momentum regime; the histogram flipped negative on 10-06 and deepened on 10-07, capturing the momentum rollover. (macds was omitted as redundant — the histogram already encodes the MACD–signal gap.)
- **rsi** — crashed from 83.7 (09-17) and a sustained >70 run through early October down to 52.5; the overbought condition has been worked off rapidly.
- **boll_ub** — bands are extremely wide (upper band at 36.01 vs. close 27.29), quantifying how far the breakout stretched price; price has re-entered the band envelope.
- **atr** — at 2.16, daily true range is ~8% of price — roughly double the ~1.0 ATR seen in early September. Essential for sizing and stops.

boll, boll_lb, vwma, and macds were deliberately left out to avoid redundancy: the verified snapshot supplies boll/boll_lb values anyway, and the mid-band is nearly coincident with current price, adding little incremental signal versus the 10 EMA.

## Detailed Trend Analysis

### 1. The long bear phase and the base (Oct 2025 – Aug 2026)
From 20.16 on 2025-10-07, SDGR bled steadily lower: an November breakdown to ~$16–17, a January collapse from ~$18.8 to ~$14, and a capitulatory flush on 2026-02-11 (close 11.98 on 5.29M volume — the heaviest down-volume day of the year, a classic selling-climax signature). The stock then spent five months carving a base roughly between $11.0 and $13.5, with a failed rally attempt in late April–May (peak close 15.20 on 05-29) that faded back to ~$15 by mid-July. The 200 SMA at 16.15 still sits above most of this base, which is why the September breakout is structurally significant — it wasn't just a bounce, it was a full regime change.

### 2. The August–September breakout
Momentum ignited on 2026-08-05–08-06 (15.65 → 17.81 on 2.74M volume), ran to ~$20.9 by early September, consolidated briefly at $18.8–$20, then exploded: 09-14 (+9.1% to 20.75), 09-15 (+12% to 23.25), 09-16 (+2.9%), and the climactic 09-17 (+26.4% to 30.24 on 9.03M shares — roughly 7–9x normal volume). This is textbook breakout-followed-by-blowoff price action. The stock then churned in a $28.5–$31 range for two weeks before pushing to $32.60 on 10-05, which proved to be a bull trap: -11.3% to 28.90 on 10-06 and -5.6% to 27.29 on 10-07.

### 3. Current indicator posture (verified snapshot, 2026-10-07)

- **Trend**: Close of 27.29 is +23% above the 50 SMA (22.17) and +69% above the 200 SMA (16.15). All averages are rising steeply — the intermediate and long-term trend is unambiguously up.
- **Short-term momentum broke**: Price closed below the 10 EMA (29.28) for the first time since the breakout began. MACD (2.37) has rolled under its signal (2.72) — histogram at -0.35 and deepening for two consecutive sessions. This is a confirmed bearish MACD crossover, the first since mid-September.
- **Momentum reset**: RSI at 52.5 is back to neutral after spending 09-15 through 10-05 almost continuously above 70 (peaked 83.7 on 09-17). The overbought risk that made chasing dangerous has been released — but note RSI fell ~22 points in two sessions, reflecting how violent the pullback is.
- **Volatility**: ATR of 2.16 means a "normal" daily move is now ~$2.15 (~8% of price). Bollinger bands span 19.38–36.01 around a 27.70 mid-band — the close at 27.29 sits just below the mid-band, i.e., price has reverted to the mean of the post-breakout range.
- **Volume character**: The two down days (10-06: 5.26M, 10-07: 4.56M) came on heavy volume — this is distribution, not a quiet drift lower. Sellers are active, not absent.

### 4. Key levels (all directly supported by the data)

- **Resistance**: 30.2–30.7 (repeated closes/ highs across 09-17 through 09-30 where price stalled), then 31.05 (09-30 close) and the 32.60–33.78 zone (10-05 close / 10-06 intraday high).
- **Support**: 26.87 (10-07 intraday low — the immediate line in the sand); below that, ~23.9–24.1 (09-16/09-17 pre-gap area, and roughly the 0.5 retracement zone of the 18.80→33.78 move sits near 26.3); the rising 50 SMA at 22.17 is the deeper trend-defining support. The Bollinger lower band at 19.38 and the 50 SMA region would only come into play on a full breakdown.
- **The 09-17 open near 24.09 also marks where the blowoff leg began** — a round-trip below ~24 would signal the breakout has failed rather than consolidated.

### 5. Actionable insights

- **Trend traders**: The primary trend is still up — price > rising 50/200 SMA by a wide margin. Pullbacks toward the 24–27 zone with stabilizing volume and a flattening MACD histogram would be the constructive re-entry scenario, with the 50 SMA (~22) as the line where the thesis must be abandoned.
- **Momentum traders**: The signal has flipped bearish short-term. MACD below signal, price below 10 EMA, and heavy distribution volume argue against buying the dip until momentum stabilizes (e.g., MACDh stops making lower lows, or RSI holds above ~40 on the next down leg).
- **Risk management is paramount**: With ATR ≈ $2.16, a standard 1×ATR stop is ~8% — far wider than normal. Position sizes should be cut roughly in half versus early-September levels to keep dollar risk constant. Chasing bounces without confirmation risks catching a falling knife; the last two sessions averaged a >$2.5 daily range.
- **Bearish scenario**: A close below 26.87 opens ~24; a close below ~24 would negate the breakout structure entirely and shift focus to the 50 SMA / lower band near 19–22.
- **Divergence watch**: The 10-05 close of 32.60 made a marginal new high while RSI (74.9) was below its 09-17 peak (83.7) — a mild bearish divergence that has now resolved to the downside. Watch whether the next bounce produces a lower MACD peak for confirmation of a larger topping process.

**Bottom line**: Structurally bullish, tactically bearish. SDGR is in the volatile digestion phase of a massive breakout. The right posture is patience — let the pullback define a floor above ~$24 before re-engaging long, and respect the elevated volatility in any sizing decision.

## Key Points Summary

The news feed returned a placeholder for the entire window. This is a tooling limitation (the feed only serves recent items), not evidence that no news exists for SDGR. No institutional framing signal can be extracted; this materially weakens the overall read.

Reading the unlabeled bodies instead:

Typical for this stock" — @scott52; "-5.6% more today with $XBI green at +0.43%" — @SunAndStorm; "short 33.7" — @BB_88_; a bearish engulfing signal flagged by @SunAndStorm). Watcher count reportedly grew (+50 new watchers, ~6478 total), suggesting rising attention during the drawdown.

### Reddit — UNAVAILABLE
Reddit search returned a placeholder for the window (same tooling limitation). No r/wallstreetbets, r/stocks, or r/investing discussion can be assessed. Silence here is absence of data, not absence of interest.

With news and Reddit both unavailable, only StockTwits carries signal, and internally it diverges: labeled sentiment skews bearish (the only tag is Bearish, plus several hostile unlabeled posts) while the most active poster cohort is explicitly accumulating the dip. There is no institutional or Reddit signal to confirm or contradict either side.

- **Dip-buying accumulation:** Repeated claims of large-volume accumulation and a price floor near €25.50–27.
- **AI/compute exposure:** SDGR is being discussed in the same breath as the compute-infrastructure narrative, and one poster notes the launch of "Tectora" as a positive signal.

- **Catalyst (unverified):** Claims of large institutional accumulation and "a bomb about to drop" are poster speculation, not events.
- **Risk:** Technical deterioration — bearish engulfing pattern, price below short-term range, one trader openly short at 33.7; sector correlation means further weakness in $XBI/genomics peers likely drags SDGR.
- **Risk:** Sentiment is being driven largely by a handful of very active accounts (@bambus3001 alone is ~10 of 30 messages), so the "bullish floor" reading may overstate breadth.

With two of three sources unavailable, this is a low-confidence read of a fractured retail board: frustration and shorts from the drawdown versus vocal conviction buyers treating it as a discount in a strong uptrend, with a dated earnings catalyst ahead. Band: Mixed, score 4.9/10 — effectively a coin-flip sentiment with a slight bearish tilt from recent price action and the hostile tone of the only tagged posts. Treat as context for the trader, not a price call.

# SDGR — Fundamental Research Report (as of 2026-10-07)

## Company Profile
Schrödinger, Inc. (SDGR) — computational chemistry/drug-discovery software and drug-development company (software licenses plus collaborative/proprietary pipeline). Note: the fundamentals vendor withheld profile-level data (market cap, multiples, 52-week range) for this date to avoid lookahead bias, and insider transactions were not available point-in-time. This report is built entirely from SEC EDGAR-filed financial statements.

## Income Statement — Revenue Growth, Persistent Operating Losses, Rare Profit Print

**Revenue (quarterly, $M):**
- 2019: ~21/19/20 (~$60M pace)
- 2021: ~30/qtr
- 2023: 65 / 35 / 43
- 2024: 37 / 47 / 35
- 2025: 60 / 55 / 54
- 2026: Q1 59, Q2 59 → ~$236M annualized, roughly flat to slightly up vs. 2025 (~$169M first 3 qtrs).

Revenue has grown steadily (~4x since 2019), driven by software licensing plus milestone/collaboration lumpiness — note the Q1 spikes (60 in 2025-Q1, 65 in 2023-Q1) typical of milestone recognition.

**Margins:**
- Gross margin: volatile (35–70%); recent quarters ~50–55% (Q2-2026: 32/59 ≈ 54%).
- Operating income: **negative every quarter in the dataset** — ~$(40)–(70)M/qtr lately. Q2-2026: $(42)M; Q1-2026: $(49)M. Opex (~$75–85M/qtr implied) far exceeds gross profit.
- Net income: persistently negative, with two notable exceptions: **Q1-2023 +$129M** (almost certainly a one-time gain — likely the Nimbus/Takeda-related or equity-method/fair-value item, not operations) and **Q2-2026 +$6M** (+$0.08 diluted EPS), the first positive quarter in ~3 years. Q2-2026's flip to profitability despite $(42)M operating loss implies a ~$48M non-operating gain (investment/fair-value/other income) — traders should treat it as non-recurring unless confirmed otherwise.

## Balance Sheet — Strong Liquidity, But Equity Eroding

- **Cash & equivalents: $288M** at 2026-06-30 — near multi-year highs (up from $172M at 2025-09-30 and $231M at 2026-03-31). Cash was rebuilt in 2026 (Q2 saw +$103M investing inflow, likely investment maturities).
- Current assets $470M vs. current liabilities $174M → **current ratio ~2.7x**, healthy.
- Total assets $640M; total liabilities $311M (down from $402M peak at 2025-03-31 — a liability reduction/deleveraging event occurred around then).
- **Stockholders' equity: $329M** — down from $624M at end-2020 and $549M at end-2023; roughly $25–45M/qtr of erosion from losses, modestly offset (equity ticked up to $364M Q1-2026 on a financing/other event, then back down).
- Minimal debt footprint: financing cash flows ~$0–3M/qtr since 2021 — the big raises were 2020 (post-IPO, ~$540M YTD).

## Cash Flow — Burn Improving but Not Solved

- Operating cash flow (YTD figures): 2022 $(95)M, 2023 $(99)M, 2024 $(126)M, **2025 improved to +$30M at 9 months** (Q1-2025 showed +$144M — large upfront/milestone collections), but **2026 back to burn: $(15)M Q1, $(49)M H1**.
- Capex trivial (~$1–3M/qtr) — asset-light software model.
- Net: business consumes ~$50–130M/yr operationally in a normal year, funded by a ~$288M cash pile plus investments. **Roughly 2+ years of runway** at recent burn — no near-term solvency risk.

## Key Risks & Data Gaps

1. Core operations have never been sustainably profitable; Q2-2026 net profit rests on non-operating gains.
2. Revenue concentration/lumpiness from milestones makes quarterly comps noisy.
3. Steady equity erosion and reliance on investment portfolio returns to offset operating losses.
4. Vendor withheld profile/valuation data and insider transactions for 2026-10-07 — no market-cap or insider-sentiment signal available in this snapshot.

## Key Points Summary

| Metric | Value / Trend | Signal |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue (Q2-2026) | $59M; ~$236M annualized | Growing slowly vs. 2025 |
| Gross margin | ~50–55% recent | Healthy software-like, volatile on mix |
| Operating income | $(42)M Q2-2026; negative every quarter | Core unprofitability persists |
| Net income Q2-2026 | +$6M (+$0.08 EPS) | Driven by ~$48M non-operating gain — likely non-recurring |
| Cash & equivalents | $288M (2026-06-30) | Strong, rebuilt in 2026 |
| Current ratio | ~2.7x | Solid short-term liquidity |
| Operating cash flow | $(49)M H1-2026 | Burn resumed after 2025's milestone-driven positive year |
| Stockholders' equity | $329M, down ~50% from 2020 peak | Persistent erosion from losses |
| Debt/financing | Minimal; no meaningful debt raises since 2020 | Low leverage |
| Data gaps | No valuation multiples, profile, or insider data at 2026-10-07 | Fundamental view only |

**Trader takeaway:** SDGR is a well-capitalized, low-leverage company with a durable software revenue base but a structurally loss-making cost base (drug-discovery R&D). The Q2-2026 profit is a quality-of-earnings flag, not a turnaround. Runway is ample; the thesis hinges on software growth outpacing R&D burn and pipeline milestones — watch whether non-operating gains repeat in Q3-2026.

Bull Analyst: # Bull Case: SDGR (Schrödinger, Inc.) — Opening Argument

Let me be direct: the bears are going to show you a two-day chart and call it a thesis. I'm going to show you a company that just executed a full secular trend reversal on 7–9x volume, holds $288M in cash against minimal debt, and sits at the intersection of the two most valuable narratives in the market right now — AI-driven compute and drug discovery. Then we can talk about whether a 16% pullback after a 55% breakout is a "sell signal" or a gift.

## 1. The Structural Story: This Is a Regime Change, Not a Bounce

The technical report — which the bears will selectively quote — actually confirms the bull thesis at every level that matters:

- **Price is +23% above the 50 SMA ($22.17) and +69% above the 200 SMA ($16.15).** Both averages are rising steeply. This is not a stock in a downtrend having a rally — this is a stock that broke out of a five-month base and completely reversed a year-long secular decline. Regime changes like this don't resolve back to $12 because of two red days.
- **The September breakout was validated by volume.** 9.03M shares on 09-17 versus a ~1M baseline. Moves on that kind of volume signature are institutional repositioning, not retail froth — and institutions don't unwind a position they built over two weeks because of a pullback to the breakout mean.
- **The pullback is mathematically normal.** The stock ran from $18.80 to $33.78 — a ~80% move. It has now retraced to $27.29, which sits almost exactly at the Bollinger mid-band ($27.70) and roughly the 0.5 retracement zone (~$26.3) of the entire breakout leg. This is textbook mean reversion within a bull structure. RSI has reset from 83.7 to a neutral 52.5 — the overbought risk that made chasing dangerous has been completely released. The bears are citing momentum indicators that just spent two days *de-risking the entry*.

## 2. The Fundamental Floor the Bears Will Ignore

Yes, SDGR loses money operationally. Now let me tell you why that matters less here than for almost any other unprofitable growth name:

- **$288M cash, minimal debt, ~2.7x current ratio.** There is no solvency risk, no forced raise coming, no dilution cliff. The burn is ~$50–130M/year against a cash pile rebuilt to multi-year highs in 2026. Compare that to the typical small-cap biotech the bears want to lump SDGR in with — SDGR has a *revenue-generating software business* funding its pipeline, not a serial dilution machine.
- **The software business is real and growing.** Revenue is ~4x its 2019 level and annualizing around $236M with ~50–55% gross margins. That's a durable, high-margin licensing base — the thing that makes SDGR fundamentally different from pure-play pipeline bets. When the market re-rates "AI for drug discovery" names, SDGR is the one with actual recurring software revenue underneath it.
- **Q2-2026 printed positive net income (+$0.08 EPS).** The bears will say it's a non-operating gain — fine, it's still evidence the investment portfolio and equity stakes are generating real value that offsets the R&D burn. That's the model working as designed.

## 3. The Narrative Tailwind: SDGR Is the Compute-Discovery Trade

Look at what the social data is actually telling us beneath the noise: SDGR is being discussed *in the same breath as the AI compute infrastructure trade* — "Jensen: 'just buy more compute.' $SDGR: 'say less.'" The market is beginning to price SDGR not as a speculative biotech but as picks-and-shovels for computational drug discovery. That's a re-rating catalyst, and re-ratings happen violently — exactly like the September move we just witnessed.

And there's a dated catalyst the bears cannot wave away: **Q3 earnings on 2026-11-04**, four weeks out. The dip-buyers positioning into that print aren't stupid money — they're front-running a quarter where another software/milestone beat or another positive surprise on the bottom line re-ignites the entire thesis.

## 4. Pre-Refuting the Bear Case

Let me take the bear arguments before they're made:

**"MACD crossed bearish, price broke the 10 EMA, heavy distribution volume."**

RSI reset to neutral, price reverted to the mid-band — the technical damage has already been done and priced. Selling here is selling the completed correction, not the beginning of one.

**"The 10Y yield is at its highest since 2002 — hostile for long-duration growth."**
This is the bears' best point and I'll still take it apart. First, yields *eased* late in the week — the headwind is already abating. Second, SDGR's September re-rating happened *into* this same rate environment, which means the market has already started pricing a company-specific catalyst strong enough to override the macro headwind. Third, SDGR carries $288M of cash earning yield — higher rates literally improve its non-operating income line, the same line that just flipped Q2 profitable.

A coin-flip sentiment read on a stock up ~140% in six months, *after* a 16% pullback, is actually constructive — the froth is gone, the weak hands capitulated ("Took my losses" is the single most bullish retail post a bull can read), and watcher count *grew* during the drawdown. Meanwhile the most active posters are accumulating with a stated floor at $25.50–27 and citing fundamentals, not memes.

**"It's a falling knife, wait for stabilization."**
I'll concede the sizing point — ATR of $2.16 demands respect. But "wait for confirmation" is how you end up buying at $31 again. The disciplined bull play is staged accumulation in the $24–27 support band with a hard thesis-invalidation level at a close below ~$24 — defined risk of ~10% against a return to the $30–33 resistance zone and beyond, with a November catalyst as the kicker.

Schrödinger is a fundamentally improved company — rebuilt cash position, growing software revenue, a profitable quarter on the books — that just completed a violent, volume-confirmed secular breakout and is now offering a technically textbook entry at the mean of the post-breakout range. The bear case is a two-day momentum chart. The bull case is the next two quarters. I know which one I'm buying.
